clauses.reason: Terminated by performance on issuance: the order's sole operative sentence ("are hereby revoked") is a one-time revocation of Executive Order No. 11697, Executive Order No. 11709 and the authority they conferred on the Department of Agriculture to inspect income tax returns; no effective-date or delay wording appears in the held text, so the revocation is read as performed on signing, 1974-03-21. Actor: EO:11773 itself, mechanism exhausted by performance. Nothing held postpones, suspends or reverses it.

research_rationale:
EO:11773 (signed 1974-03-21; 39 FR 10881, Federal Register of March 22, 1974) revokes Executive Order No. 11697 of January 17, 1973 and Executive Order No. 11709 of March 27, 1973, and the authority those orders gave the Department of Agriculture to inspect income tax returns. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's one clause is the sole operative sentence; the text holds no other command. The revocation is a one-time command performed when the order was signed: its own text ("are hereby revoked") uses the present-tense words of immediate effect and contains no effective-date, delay or condition wording, so I read it as taking effect on signing, 1974-03-21. A performed revocation exhausts the command; that the revoked order or authority is gone is a surviving consequence, not a continuing duty of this order. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held texts that cite it are its own Federal Register printing. I found no held order that revokes, amends or suspends it.
